segmente.text: How to sell anything to anyone.
A yogurt that says 20% fat is the same as one that says 80% fat free,
but the second version sounds more appealing.
People buy based on how information is framed.
Instead of selling one bag and one watch for $49,
say buy a bag for $49 and get a new watch for free.
The second option feels like a better deal.
A button that says buy now doesn't feel urgent.
But if you say only a few left in stock,
people feel more eager to buy.
The fear of missing out motivates people to act fast.
